letters.title: An envelope with your name on it
letters.preview: Yes, someone built a mailbox instead of sending a text.
pages: Okay, here's the situation. I could have sent a message. A normal person would have sent a message. Instead, there's a mailbox, a flower shop and a suspiciously enthusiastic suitcase.

It's not because every day needs a grand gesture. Mostly, I wanted you to have somewhere to wander into when you feel like it. On a good day, a strange day, or a day when you have exactly zero interesting things to report.
You don't have to do anything here. Even opening this letter counts as excellent use of the facilities. — Your friend on the other side of the map.

letters.title: In defence of ordinary Tuesdays
letters.preview: Big days have photographers, cake, and people making speeches. Ordinary Tuesdays.
pages: Big days have photographers, cake, and people making speeches. Ordinary Tuesdays have traffic, unanswered messages and maybe one decent cup of tea. Unfair, really.
But I like the ordinary stuff. A ridiculous thing you noticed. A random photo. A conversation that begins with 'you won't believe this' and turns out to be about absolutely nothing.
If nothing extraordinary happened today, you can still tell me about it.

letters.title: The fifth time? Suspicious.
letters.preview: Five visits. I had not prepared an award ceremony for this, which is deeply unpro.
pages: Five visits. I had not prepared an award ceremony for this, which is deeply unprofessional of me.
I hope something in this room felt familiar the second or third time. Maybe you kept a postcard. Maybe you made a catastrophically bad cup of digital chai. Maybe you just visited the flowers.
Either way, you're always welcome back. There is, tragically, still no actual cake.

letters.title: A page that deserves real handwriting
letters.preview: I originally wanted to put a handwritten page here. A proper one, with crossing-o.
pages: I originally wanted to put a handwritten page here. A proper one, with crossing-outs and all the untidy bits that make handwriting human.
That part deserves to be real, not a computer pretending to hold a pen. Until I can put an actual handwritten letter in the mailbox, consider this one a promise of better stationery.

letters.title: A letter for later-later
letters.preview: Oh, hello from the future. 2027 sounded far away when I started building this. Th.
pages: Oh, hello from the future. 2027 sounded far away when I started building this. Then calendars did their usual trick.

I don't know what your world looks like now, or which cities you've crossed off your wish list. I hope there have been new places, wonderful unexpected days, and people who make you laugh at the worst possible moments.
And I hope this old room still makes sense to open sometimes.

letters.title: When your battery is at 3%
letters.preview: If you're tired, I'm not going to turn this into a five-step improvement plan. Yo.
pages: If you're tired, I'm not going to turn this into a five-step improvement plan. You probably have enough people explaining how to optimise a day.
Find something comfortable. Ignore an unnecessary notification. Let something wait until tomorrow if it can.
You can leave this letter half-read. I won't report you to the stationery authorities.

letters.title: When you miss home
letters.preview: Rain, distance and the bits of home a map cannot hold.
pages: There are some things a map can't fit: the sound of a particular house, a smell from a kitchen, the way Kerala rain changes everything for an hour.
Being away doesn't make those things smaller. And missing one place doesn't mean you can't build a good life somewhere else.
If you feel like talking about home, even the completely ordinary parts, I'm listening.

letters.title: When you have great news
letters.preview: Stop reading and tell me everything.
pages: Excuse me. You have GOOD NEWS and you're reading a letter instead of telling me? An investigation will be launched.
I want the whole story. The unnecessary introduction, the moment you found out, the reaction that made absolutely no sense and whatever came next.
Seriously, I'm glad something good found you.

letters.title: When something big is tomorrow
letters.preview: The night before something important is a ridiculous time. Suddenly the clock get.
pages: The night before something important is a ridiculous time. Suddenly the clock gets loud, every decision feels permanent, and your brain asks questions at 1:43 a.m.
I can't tell you how tomorrow will go. I can tell you that you don't have to solve every possibility tonight.
Keep what you need nearby. Ask questions if you have them. I'll be rooting for you without making a big speech about it.

letters.title: When sleep is avoiding you
letters.preview: So your brain has opened a conference when everybody else has gone home. Very inc.
pages: So your brain has opened a conference when everybody else has gone home. Very inconsiderate management.
I won't tell you to 'just sleep', because that is spectacularly useless advice. Maybe lower the brightness, listen to some rain, or read something wonderfully boring.
There is no need to reply. I'm only leaving the light on in this corner of the internet.

letters.title: When your brain opens 47 tabs
letters.preview: I've been informed there's a committee meeting in your head, and the agenda has f.
pages: I've been informed there's a committee meeting in your head, and the agenda has forty-seven items.
Not all of them need a decision today. Especially the imaginary conversations where you predict everyone's exact reaction. Those are frankly exhausting even as a spectator.
If you want to explain the chaos out loud sometime, I'll bring tea and appropriately unhelpful jokes.

letters.title: When you need a laugh
letters.preview: Congratulations. You've been appointed head of a completely fictional airport. Ev.
pages: Congratulations. You've been appointed head of a completely fictional airport. Every flight is delayed because a passenger has packed three extra opinions and a suitcase full of snacks.
The only employee is a tired pigeon named Suresh. He has submitted his resignation twice but cannot work the printer.
I know this story makes no sense. That's exactly why the pigeon has a pension.

letters.title: When you feel stuck
letters.preview: People say 'take the next step' as if steps come with helpful glowing arrows pain.
pages: People say 'take the next step' as if steps come with helpful glowing arrows painted on them.
Sometimes you don't know what the next step is. Sometimes you know and don't feel like taking it. Both situations are embarrassingly human.
You don't have to turn every quiet patch into a breakthrough. I can keep you company in the middle bit.

letters.title: When you finish something big
letters.preview: Hold on. You finished it? Whatever the thing was, I hope you gave yourself a mome.
pages: Hold on. You finished it? Whatever the thing was, I hope you gave yourself a moment before immediately looking for the next task.
I'm picturing a very serious award being presented by a very small and unqualified committee. The certificate is written on the back of a grocery receipt.
For real, I'm happy for you. Tell me how it went.

letters.title: When it is raining
letters.preview: Rain in Kerala has a very different personality from rain elsewhere. Sometimes it.
pages: Rain in Kerala has a very different personality from rain elsewhere. Sometimes it feels like the whole neighbourhood has stopped to listen.
There is a rainy window in the Quiet Corner if you want one. No dramatic soundtrack required.
If you're standing near an actual window, though, the original is usually better.

letters.title: When it is your birthday
letters.preview: Happy birthday, Maha. I considered writing something elegant and mature, but I kn.
pages: Happy birthday, Maha. I considered writing something elegant and mature, but I know neither of us would trust that version.
I hope there is good food, at least one absurd conversation, and a photo you will later insist is terrible even though everyone else likes it.
Most of all, I hope the day is yours, not some performance for everybody else.

letters.title: When you post your first vlog
letters.preview: You posted your first travel vlog? Wait. This is an event. Where is the premiere?.
pages: You posted your first travel vlog? Wait. This is an event. Where is the premiere? Who approved the poster? Is there a badly designed fan club I can join?
I hope you kept the parts that felt like you: the awkward cut, the unexpected detour, the beautiful thing you almost forgot to film.
You did the hard part. You actually started. Now please send me the link so I can become insufferable about it.

letters.title: When you forget who you are
letters.preview: I could list a hundred grand things I think about you, but I suspect you'd roll y.
pages: I could list a hundred grand things I think about you, but I suspect you'd roll your eyes before number four.
So here's something smaller. You're allowed to change, get things wrong, want something different, and still be the same person I like hearing from.
You don't owe the world a perfect explanation of who you're becoming.

letters.title: When you miss me
letters.preview: Oh? You miss me? I will need this remarkable statement signed and witnessed. A sc.
pages: Oh? You miss me? I will need this remarkable statement signed and witnessed. A screenshot is acceptable.
I'm joking. Mostly. Distance is strange that way: sometimes everything feels normal, and sometimes one silly thing happens and you wish the other person were there to laugh at it.
You can send me the silly thing. I'll probably have an even sillier response.

letters.title: For a big day
letters.preview: Just a note for a day that matters. Keep the practical things close: what you nee.
pages: Just a note for a day that matters. Keep the practical things close: what you need, whom to ask, and the questions you want answered.
You don't have to be brave for anyone watching. You can be nervous, quiet, annoyed, or all three in the same hour.
Wishing you an easier day and good people around you. I'll be thinking of you.
